name: English
title: RiftLauncher
description: RiftLauncher is an independent launcher for Vintage Story. Install multiple versions, keep separate installations with their own mods, worlds and configs, and make backups.
headline: Every version of Vintage Story, side by side.
lead: Keep as many installations as you like, each with its own mods, worlds and configs, make manual and automatic backups before anything breaks, and browse the ModDB without leaving the launcher.
beta: Beta prerelease, so expect rough edges. Back up your worlds first.
about: RiftLauncher is built on {vsLauncher:VS Launcher} by {xurxo:XurxoMF}, and carries it on now that the original is archived.
Made by the {stratum:Stratum} team, with its core rebuilt and tested on Windows and Linux.
Thanks to XurxoMF and everyone who coded, translated and tested the original. The {contributors:contributors page} names them.

featuresIntro: A line or two per area. The documentation goes further.
cards: Install any official version in one click, or register a game folder you already have. Two builds of the same version each get a name you can change later.
Each installation picks its version and keeps its own mods, worlds, settings and environment variables, so what you do in one leaves the others alone.
Make a backup by hand whenever you want, or have the launcher take one before every play, with a limit you set.
Export an installation's mods as a .json file, and import one to install them all at once.
Save a server's address on an installation, and Join starts the game already pointed at it. A modpack can carry the bookmark to whoever you share it with.
Keep several Vintage Story accounts saved and switch between them. No system keyring? You can still log in, and login works behind a proxy.

trust: The {privacy:privacy policy} lists every request the launcher can make, and ships inside it under Info & Help.
Shared logs and reports hide your folder paths and account details.
The launcher can count your install on its ModDB page, and it asks first.
It asks once per version, and you can answer for good either way.
Every installer is built by a public CI run from a tagged commit.
Each release lists SHA-256 checksums and VirusTotal results.
Every change goes through a reviewed {prs:pull request} and thousands of automated tests.
Bugs are tracked in the open on the {issues:issue tracker}.
installIntro: The files below come from the newest release, and every older one is on the {releases:GitHub releases page}. RiftLauncher is a launcher, not a mod: never put it in your Mods folder.
installWindows: Run the setup .exe. It is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn: the checksums and scans are on the release. Vintage Story needs .NET 7, 8 or 10 depending on the version.
installLinux: The AppImage runs on any distribution, and the .deb, .rpm and .pacman packages install like any other app. The built-in updater handles every one of them.
installMac: No build yet. Follow the {releases:releases} to know when that changes.
installNotes: On first run, RiftLauncher copies your VS Launcher settings into its own folder, so your installations show up right away. Your account usually comes across too; if not, you log in once. Nothing on the VS Launcher side is moved or removed.
The launcher checks for its own updates and asks before downloading one. Betas are opt-in under Config, Beta versions, and What's new shows after an update.
newRelease: {tag} is out: read the notes on GitHub
downloadsNote: Counted from the installers on each GitHub release when this page was built, then refreshed in your browser from the GitHub API when the page loads. Fresh downloads and automatic updates both count, so a bar reads as how many installs moved onto that version, not as new players.
overTimeNote: {firstTotal} on {firstDate} to {lastTotal} on {lastDate}, counted once a day.
